title: Baking Cakes
strapline: Weigh, mix, spoon and wait — the magic of watching batter rise into cakes to share.
intent: Children follow a real recipe from start to finish, learning sequence, care and patience.
Children weigh, count and measure with a genuine purpose — grams of flour, number of eggs, spoons of sugar.
Children observe an irreversible change: liquid batter becomes solid, risen cake in the heat.
Children build hand strength through mixing, beating, spooning and decorating.
Children experience the deep pleasure of making something to share with others.
implementation: Use a simple, picture-based recipe and let children read the steps and do the real jobs.
Weigh ingredients on scales and count them in — 'three eggs, crack and count', 'two spoons of sugar'.
Talk about the change: batter is runny, but the heat makes it rise and set — and it can't go back.
Give everyone real mixing and beating to do, building strength and taking turns with the bowl.
Share the sharing — cases to fill fairly, cakes to count out one each, decorating to make them theirs.
Bring in the waiting and the anticipation: watch through the oven door, and mark the time.
Talk about celebrations and the cakes families make, and who these cakes are for.
key_questions: What do we need to do first, and what comes next in the recipe?
How many eggs shall we crack — can you count them in?
What do you think will happen to the batter in the oven?
How can we share the cake cases so everyone gets the same?
Who shall we make these cakes for?

impact.text: Children follow a real recipe in sequence, with care and patience, from start to finish.
Children weigh, count and measure ingredients with a genuine purpose.
Children observe and talk about the irreversible change from batter to risen cake.
Children mix, beat, spoon and decorate, building hand strength and control.
Children share the cakes out fairly and take pride in making something for others.
Children connect baking to celebrations and the food their families make.

enhancements: A simple picture recipe on a stand at child height.
Scales, measuring spoons and bowls for real weighing.
Whisks, wooden spoons and cases for mixing and filling.
Decorating trays — icing, sprinkles, fruit — for making each cake their own.
A timer and a view of the oven for the exciting wait.
Aprons and a proper handwashing routine before cooking.
A cake stand and plates for sharing at the end.

playing_exploring: Children explore the ingredients with all their senses as they mix.
They discover what beating and folding does to the batter.
active_learning: Children wait, watch and persist through a process with a delayed, delicious reward.
They take turns beating the stiff mixture, putting in real effort.
creating_thinking: Children predict what will happen in the oven and check by watching.
They decide who the cakes are for and how to decorate and share them.
